focus: correctness — concurrency between two sessions on the packet log

findingDetails.title: Per-packet log lock is scoped to the state directory, so two sessions with different state directories silently lose log rows
findingDetails.evidence: appendGoalLog locks only the state directory (`withFileLocks(goalScope.stateDir, [packetLockName(...)])` at goal-core.cjs:1050); the lock name carries workspace plus packet path (:894-896) but the directory comes from resolveStateDir (:151-162), which honors the OPENCODE_GOAL_STATE_DIR override. Two writers with different state dirs never contend: each reads goal.md, inserts its row, passes the durable-slice guard (:1069-1073) and renames its copy into place (:899-920), so the second write discards the first row. Reproduced through the shipped CLI on a fixture packet under this lineage: both sessions on the same state dir landed both rows (positive control), while 20 concurrent pairs with state dirs state-a/state-b survived only 9 x-rows and 11 y-rows, every process reporting STATUS=OK ACTION=log.
findingDetails.impact: Log rows are lost silently whenever the two writers do not share a state directory; the hook README advertises the append as serialized under a per-packet lock (README.md:60). Trigger needs the documented test/probe override, so P2.
findingDetails.recommendation: Derive the lock directory from the packet workspace, or document the state-dir precondition beside the serialization claim. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Lock acquisition, lock naming, state-dir resolution, the write path and the guard read directly; loss reproduced end to end with the shipped CLI and a same-directory positive control.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: Cross-runtime goal contract with a shared slice module, a parallel plugin implementation, a validator measurement boundary, per-runtime adapters and a packet that claims the fixes.

targetSelection.selectionReason: The lock, the append path and the CLI router are the producer, the operator surface and the documented claim for the concurrency question the scope names.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Two sessions appending to one packet serialize on one lock.

searchActions.queryOrPath: two CLI processes, same state dir vs divergent state dirs, 20 pairs
searchActions.result: Same dir: both rows land. Divergent dirs: 9 of 20 and 11 of 20 rows survive; both sides report STATUS=OK.

searchLedger.rationale: The lock's directory, not its name, decides contention, and the documented override splits the directory.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The scope lock and the packet lock can nest and deadlock.

searchActions.result: Each acquires exactly one lock; no nesting.
